rationale: The source names Samaria, Esria and Mareroth; the Chronicles sequence contains differing names and repeated Amariah/Azariah generations. Exact personal equivalences and omitted generations are not established by silently normalizing the names.

The source names Zaraia, Saouia and Bokki; Chronicles has Bokai, Ozi and Zaraia. The comparable position in the Aaronic ancestry does not resolve the differing middle name into an exact sequence of personal identities.
Zathoes in the later list is not silently substituted for Zathoua in the earlier list. The actual family-name forms and distinct group counts are preserved pending secure identification.
Elam in the later return is not automatically identified with Ailam rather than the additional Elam-ar entry at Ezra 2:31. Neither precise family equivalence nor individual identity is resolved.

The later sons of Ioab are not automatically equated with the earlier sons of Ioab named inside the Phaathmoab group. The exact subgroup relationship and membership across returns remain unestablished.
Baani in the later list is not silently normalized to Banoui in the earlier list; a secure family identity is not established by the similar names alone.
The source form Bago and the earlier Bagoi are preserved as written; this pass does not turn their resemblance into an independently established family identification.

The priestly Eram entry may invite comparison with the earlier priestly Erem, but the text also has a non-priestly Eram family. This pass preserves the spellings and does not resolve the priestly-family equation or identify its members.
Both entries include a Levite named Iozabad, but only the earlier delivery notice gives the patronymic son of Iesous. Shared name and office do not establish that the offender is that individual.
The sons of Elam are not automatically assigned to the earlier Ailam entry rather than Elam-ar at Ezra 2:31. The listed personal names do not resolve that family correspondence.
Esam is not silently normalized to Asem in the earlier inventory; neither exact family correspondence nor identities of the listed men are established from similar spelling.
